item.title: The European Union Official Promoting a Parallel ‘Board of Peace’
item.description: Dubravka Suica’s appointment in 2024 as Europe’s first Commissioner for the Mediterranean has propelled her into a high-profile post, co-leading the Palestine Donor Group, which is weaving its way around US President Trump’s flailing Board of Peace and could become a rival if the board collapses. At the second meeting of the Palestine Donor Group ... Read more

item.title: UN chief, Red Cross renew call for rules on lethal autonomous weapons
item.description: Amid unconfirmed reports that fully autonomous and AI-guided drones are now being used on the battlefield, UN chief António Guterres and the President of the Red Cross on Tuesday renewed their urgent call for stricter global controls, before it is too late.

item.title: Land degradation is costing far more than restoring: UN deputy chief
item.description: Countries are spending too little to restore degraded land even as the economic cost of doing nothing climbs towards $1 trillion a year, UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed warned at a major UN land conference in Mongolia.

item.title: Japan’s ‘2050 Weather Forecast’ highlights extreme heat in the future
item.description: As extreme heat becomes an increasingly visible reality across Japan, meteorologists, scientists, businesses and professional footballers are joining forces to encourage stronger climate action and raise awareness of the risks posed by global warming.

item.title: Rohingyas in Myanmar suffering ‘heartbreaking’ misery and cruelty
item.description: Members of the minority ethnic Rohingya Muslim group in Myanmar are “suffering, misery, and cruelty on multiple levels and across the country that is heartbreaking,” according to the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

item.title: One million children in Afghanistan face deadly malnutrition
item.description: Some 3.7 million children in Afghanistan are suffering from wasting, one of the most dangerous forms of malnutrition, with around one million currently battling the most severe, life-threatening form of the condition.

item.title: As wars spread, the global food system unravels
item.description: A family with four children abandoned its farm in Somalia after armed groups arrived and demanded payments for the right to continue cultivating the land. They walked roughly 100 kilometers to a displacement camp. One of the children died along the way.

item.title: Haiti ramps up the fight against gangs in the capital, but violence spreads elsewhere
item.description: The killings in Kenscoff began late Sunday, when armed men descended on the farming community in the hills overlooking Haiti’s capital, setting homes ablaze and attacking residents. By Monday, bodies lay in the streets and survivors were searching for missing relatives.

item.title: Colombia Declares State of Emergency Following Deadly Earthquake
item.description: Over the past week, the humanitarian crisis in Colombia has deteriorated significantly following the Mw 7.4–7.5 earthquake that struck the Chocó department on August 10. item.title: South Africa’s Anti-Immigrant Violence Slows SDG Goals, Rips Apart Africans’ Free Movement Call
item.description: The xenophobic protests against Malawians, Nigerians, Zimbabweans, and other Africans in South Africa not only created a humanitarian crisis but also jeopardised the achievement of some SDGs.
